header_sentences: See Angelic Spirit, Evil Spirit, Good Spirit, Holy Spirit, and World of Spirits.
See also Angel, Animal Spirit, After Death, Body, Brain, Genii, Inspire, Novitiate, Obsess, Siren, Society, Soul, Speak, Sphere, Subject.
Footnote:  All statements relating to the speech of Spirits among themselves, and to man's speech with Spirits, are fully quoted see Speak, from beginning to end.

contexts.text: (Emanuel Swedenborg was constantly with Spirits and Angels.)
I have been instructed about different kinds of Spirits.
The spirit of God () = the mercy of the Lord. AC 24. ( = the Divine truth. AR 200:2.)
Spirits in knowledge without love are in such a frigid life and obscure light...
Man is ruled... through Angels and Spirits.

With every man there are at least two Spirits, and two Angels; through the Spirits he has communication with the World of Spirits, through the Angels, with Heaven. Without (this) communication, he could not live. (Continued. See Angel.) (Compare AC 697.)
Man... could have spoken with Spirits and Angels... for he is one with them, because he is a Spirit clothed with a body.
As soon as corporeal things recede, the way is (again) opened, and the man is among Spirits, and shares life with them.
Spirit, or life, likened to wind. Explained, Illustrated.
(During resuscitation) I was removed from communication with Spirits in the World of Spirits, because they supposed I had departed from the life of the body.
He is then made aware that he is a Spirit. (His first experiences as such.) HH 450.
What (such) believe concerning the Spirit. (Fully stated.)
Thus they deny there is a Spirit. AC 206.
Philosophers speak about the Spirit in terms they do not understand. Described. AC 446:end.
He was translated among celestial Spirits. Described.
On the life of a soul, or Spirit. General article.
When told that he is a Spirit, he is astounded, both because he is exactly like a man... and because he had not believed there is a Spirit, or that a Spirit could be such.
A Spirit has much more excellent faculties. Described. But Spirits are not aware of this until reflection is given them. AC 1389.
(The exquisite bodily sense of Spirits, fully described.) AC 1514.
(The excellence of their mental faculties and speech, fully described.)
It is the Spirit which sensates in the body. Explained. AC 447:end.
He had believed that the Spirit would live an obscure life. Described.

One who had believed that the Spirit is not extended... I asked what he thought now about himself... He said that the Spirit is thought. (Emanuel Swedenborg shows him that even thought implies an organic substance.)
The learned believe that a Spirit is abstract thought. Explained. Thus that it will vanish when they die.

I spoke with Spirits... that men do not believe in a Spirit because they do not see it... or apprehend it... thus deny its extension, and that it is a substance... that it is in a place, consequently in the human body... The Spirits, who were simple, marvelled...

A recent Spirit asked me, What is a Spirit? supposing himself a man. I told him there is a Spirit in every man, and that as to his life man is a Spirit. Explained... I told him that he was now a Soul, or Spirit, which he might know from the fact that he was over my head... He then fled away, crying, I am a Spirit, I am a Spirit. SE 2288.
A Jew, when shown that he was a Spirit, persisted that he was a man, because he could see and hear. AC 941:2.
A Spirit applied himself to my left side, asking how he could enter Heaven...
(Another) recent Spirit desired Heaven. (His anguish on feeling it.) (See also AC 538-548. AC 1398.)
My Spirit shall not reprove man... () = an internal dictate... also the influx of truth and good.
The Most Ancient Church had... consort with Spirits and Angels.
No breath in the midst of it () nothing celestial and spiritual.
The breath of lives. Explained. (Compare AC 94.) AC 805.
A wind of storms () = the desolation of falsity.
(Since the most ancient times) many have spoken with Spirits and Angels, as Moses... but in an entirely different wav.
Whatever a Spirit thinks, those near at once know...
At first (such) do not know they are Spirits.
A phalanx of Spirits rising from Gehenna...
Cohorts of Spirits wander about, whom other Spirits greatly fear. Described.
Suppose Spirits to have no sense...
Spirits (also) have an external, (an interior, and an internal man). AC 1718:end.
A. Spirit is known from his ideas. Described.
Spirits can give others heat.
Their interior man, or Spirit, was joined to Heaven by internal respiration.
If the Lord had not come... no Spirit could have been with man: yet he cannot live a moment unless Spirits and Angels are with him.
Otherwise these Spirits would have been suffocated, although they would have revived, but after torture.
All Spirits and Angels are near enough to be seen, but no more come into view than the Lord permits.
Spirits of whom others are thinking... when the Lord permits, are present. Described.
The Spirits around me (then) appeared to be removed, and were seen below me, yet I could hear them.
The breath of His lips () = doctrine.
I spoke with Spirits about the idea of place and distance with them. Explained.
Spirits to whom bodily and earthly ideas adhere...
Such Spirits can scarcely be brought to believe that they are not living in the body.
All Spirits and Angels keep constantly in their own situation...
Spirits appear in a place where they are not. Explained.
Spirits, as Spirits, as to the organic things which constitute their bodies, are not in the place where they are seen, but may be far away. Explained.
(Thus) the walkings and translations of Spirits... are nothing but changes of state. Explained.
Spirits can be translated on high in a moment... and in the same moment deep down; and also from one end of the universe to the other. Described.
The perception of Spirits and Angels. General article.
Spirits of the scarfskin. Described.
So long as Spirits suppose that they (do everything) from themselves, they cannot have perception.
Man derives (this) from the nature of Spirits, thus from man's spirit, and its communication with the World of Spirits.
Hence such a perception reigns universally among Spirits.
There is (such) a communication that one Spirit supposes he has known what another knows... Some Spirits retain it; others do not.
A Spirit who wanted to arrogate merit (was detected) from afar. Described.

Every Spirit has communication with the interior and the inmost Heaven, although quite unaware of it: otherwise he could not live. His interior quality is known by the Angels who are in his interiors, and through those Angels he is ruled by the Lord. Thus there are communications of his interiors in Heaven, as of his exteriors in the World of Spirits. Explained.
Man's spirit is greatly delighted with knowledge... It is its food...
Under Sphere, see this reference. AC 1510. AC 1520.
Spirits said they have not the sense of taste. Explained.
Spirits and Angels have every sense, except taste, far more perfect than man ever has. (Their world described.) AC 1880. AC 1973.
Under Angel, see this reference.
(Yet) unless Spirits were organic, and Angels were organic substances, they could not speak, etc.
The things there are adapted to the senses of Spirits and Angels; for Spirits cannot see a whit of the things (here).
As Spirits are perfected, their abodes are changed into more beautiful ones. Described.
Spirits are very indignant at (the ideas men have about them). AC 1881.
On the speech of Spirits and Angels. General article. (Fully quoted under Speak, from AC 1635-1649. And also from AC 1757-1764.)

Certain (learned) Spirits... were brought into a state of thought similar to what they had had here... They then said that it is a phantasy to believe that anyone can speak with Spirits. (This shows) how difficult it is for men to believe that speaking with Spirits is possible... The reason is that they do not believe there are Spirits, still less that they themselves will come among them...
I perceive... where the Spirits are... over head, or below; at the right, or the left; at the ear, or at some other point near or inside the body; and at what distance. Explained.
These (angelic representatives) are the things which inflow into the ideas of Spirits.
For every man is ruled by the Lord through Spirits. AC 2025:end. AC 2121:2.
This kind of persuasions is not so deadly, yet they cause much discomfort to Spirits...
Such Spirits excite in man nothing but confirmations of falsity. Described.
How man may know whether he is ruled by such Spirits.
Such is the influx of Spirits with man.
All Spirits (there) are distinguished in this way. Explained. (So also) man can know among which kind he is.
Spirits who do not inflow in a stream-like way, but by vibrations and reciprocations as it were linear. (Continued. See Speak.)
These Spirits are separated from others: they induce a pain in the head, as if from the suction of an air-pump.

A Spirit came to me not long after his decease, (for) he did not know he was in the other life... He was taken up on high... and spoke with me thence... I was reading (the Word). He said he perceived nothing of the sense of the letter; but (indescribable) wonders in the spiritual sense. Described.
Other (incredulous) Spirits were taken up, and confessed it was so. Described. AC 1771. AC 3474. SE 2053.
Spirits who (here) had been delighted with the Word, have a delightful heavenly heat. Described.
Spirits who do not Want to bear about the interiors of the Word. Described.
The interior man, or spirit itself, is from the father...
Spirits spoke about the internal sense...

(The speech of Spirits among themselves, and with men. See Speak, and at AC 2470. AC 2477. AC 2733. AC 2751. AC 3342. AC 4652. AC 6996:2. AC 8734. SE 1888. SE 2142. SE 2308. SE 2868. SE 2869. SE 3050. SE 3128. SE 4335. SE 4342. SE 4865. SE 4866. SE 5557. SE 5585. SE 5588. SE 5772. SE 5787.)
Spirits, and still less Angels, cannot see anything in this world... with the sight of the spirit. Explained.
But Spirits and Angels, when the Lord pleases, can see the things in this world through the eyes of a man (whom the Lord permits) to speak with them. Example(s), AC 1954.
I was forbidden to tell (people that their departed friends saw them through my eyes) because... at heart they did not believe there are Spirits...
Spirits and Angels were astounded when they first saw through my eyes, and were affected with a new joy on account of this communication...
With other men, Spirits and Angels do not see a whit... but only perceive the thoughts and affections of those with whom they are.
Being carried by the spirit into another place. Explained. AC 1884, Explained.
Preface [3]. Man is a Spirit clothed with a body. AC 1970.
Common Spirits perceive man's thoughts (and memory) better than the man himself; angelic Spirits the still more interior things of his thoughts; and Angels... the causes and ends. AC 2488. Explained.
(Useless Spirits who hang down their hands. Described.)
Spirits who induce illusory visions. Explained. SE 1752.
The visions of enthusiastic Spirits. Explained.
When the internal sight is opened... not only the representatives, but also the Spirits themselves are seen, together with a perception of who they are, etc.
Through intermediate Spirits.
How Spirits are affected by the things which they see; and how evil Spirits are tortured when they cannot see and hear as others do. AC 1974, Example(s).
Spirits have no sense of taste; but instead an appetite for learning, which is their food. Their anguish when this food is taken away. AC 3114.
(Dreams are according to the state of the Spirits around us. See Dream.)
In the Ancient Church, Spirits who reproved and afterwards comforted were often heard. They called them God Shaddai. Explained.

The Spirits who are with man are (now, before the Last Judgment), more excited than ever to bring malignant things upon him; insomuch that the Angels can scarcely avert them, but are compelled to inflow into man more remotely.
For man is ruled through Spirits, with whom those in the World of Spirits have communication.
There appeared Spirits so black in a black cloud that I was horrified; and afterwards, others not so horrible. Explained.
Such Spirits are driven into a state... in which they do not think in Society, Described, Explained.
Such a desire (to lead others to think and speak) is innate in Spirits.
The interior memory is proper to the spirit of man.
Would it be advantageous for Spirits to use the exterior memory? (Fully quoted under Memory, here, and at AC 2478. HH 256.)
A recent Spirit indignant because he could not remember more. (Fully Explained under Memory.) AC 2481.
Spirits who relate to the interior memory.
Sight is (really) of the spirit, which sees through the eye. Explained.
The things of the body cannot enter into those of the Spirit; but the reverse, (because compounds cannot enter into simples).
Spirits reason much more fully and acutely than men...
For recent Spirits have with them the idea of natural things...
While man is in the body, he lives in Heaven as to his spirit...
For few believe they have a spirit which will live after death.
To be born of the Spirit () = of the Celestial of faith.
A Spirit who had been a general, and an adulterer. Described.
A lascivious Spirit who had extinguished in himself all desire for marriage and offspring.
Adulterous Spirits seeking a house into which to insinuate themselves. Described.
(Such Spirits) are kept in Hell lest they should come among those Spirits who are with men.
Such representatives are continual with Spirits. Described.
Spirits from another orb. AC 3348. AC 4799.
The Most Ancients were together with Spirits and Angels.
All things are disposed through the Spirits and Angels with man.
Seven Spirits sent forth into all the earth () = holy preachings of Divine truths.
Recent Spirits torment themselves about...
Soul = affection of truth; spirit, affection of good.
This Divine disposition is made by the Lord, by means of Spirits and Angels.
The body is only the covering of the spirit, and when it is put off, the spirit appears; but in a quite different form when the man has been regenerated. Described.
The representatives with Spirits. Explained.
Spirits falling upon me. Explained.
Spirits who are solely in the things of the light of the world...
For a Spirit also has a natural life; for his spiritual life is terminated in a natural one. Explained.
For man is a Spirit clothed with a body. AC 3527.
How man may know that he has a spirit in him.
The spirit of (such a one) is bright and beautiful... But the spirit of (such a one) is black and ugly.
The Ancients had communication with Spirits and Angels. (See Speak.)
Man knows these things (from) the life of his spirit... He has such knowledge from the perception of his spirit.
There are Spirits in the way who reject the ideas of evil and falsity...
All Spirits and Angels appear to themselves as men. (The reason explained.)
As to his spirit he is in Heaven.
(Sailor and rustic Spirits like machines. Their restoration to human life by the Angels.)
Such things are adapted to the apprehension... of Angels, and also to that of Spirits; for their thoughts are not interrupted (by) earthly things. Described.
But Spirits and Angels do not think like man. Explained.
(Thus) there are Spirits who are rational, who think spiritually; and (the reverse).
According to the idea of Spirits, this is called...
Spirits themselves are forms, that is, they consist of continuous forms, equally as do men, but from purer things...

Hence is the insanity of our age: that men do not believe they have a spirit in them which will live after death... when yet it is a substance much more real than the material substance of its body; nay, the spirit, after being loosed from corporeal things, is that very purified body which many say they will have at the Last Judgment.
That Spirits, or, what is the same. Souls, have a body. Described.
A Spirit who... supposed he knew everything...
Such as Spirits had been (here), such they are there. Explained.
A Spirit who came unawares and inflowed into my head...
Spirits are known by their influx into different parts of the body.

This Spirit had been taken from the Spirits with a learned man still living (here)... Communication was given through this intermediate Spirit with the thought of that man (and the Spirit tells Emanuel Swedenborg what that man's ideas are about Heaven, etc.).
One of these Spirits (over head) let himself down to me. He had been a pope. (He states his ideas about the keys, etc.).
(Spirits can easily be let into the state of life they had had here.)

The Spirit which entered into the dry bones () = the Lord's life, which when it inflows into the good of a man which he seems to himself to will and do from proprium, causes the good to be vivified...
For Spirits and Angels have a sonorous voice. (Their singing, described.)
For men, Spirits, and Angels are nothing but... forms recipient of life from the Lord.
What proceeds from the Lord... is not in Him, but from Him, and causes men. Spirits, and Angels to come forth...
(By death) man passes from shade to light, because... from the things of the body to those of the spirit.
The Divine Spiritual which proceeds from Him is called the Spirit of truth. It is holy truth, and is not of any Spirit, but of the Lord through a Spirit sent by Him. Illustrated.

How the Lord reduces the Natural to correspondence with the man of man's interior, that is, with that which will live after death of the body, and is then called the man's Spirit, which when loosed from the body, has with it all things of the external man, except the bones and flesh.
Spirits of the dura mater. Described.
All Spirits and Angels may be known from the Lord's prayer. Explained.
These Spirits could serve the Angels as mediums; for there are intermediate Spirits between the Heavens, through whom is communication. Described.
Tranquil Spirits of the sinuses of the brain. Described.
The Spirits of the ventricles of the brain. Described. AC 4050.
The Spirits of the isthmus of the brain... said they were men. I replied that they were not men endowed with bodies, but Spirits, and thus also men. Explained. AC 5189, Described. SE 3822-3837.
Spirits lament that man does not know... that they are with him... Yet (everything) of his thought and will comes through them... and through them the Lord rules the human race...
Doubts and denials are excited by the Spirits adjoined to the man.
So far as man is initiated into heavenly things... the Spirits in worldly things are removed, (otherwise) truths are dissipated.
Good, middle, and evil Spirits are adjoined to a regenerating man. Explained. (Continued. See Separate.)

As soon as Spirits come to man and enter into bis affection, they know no otherwise than that all things of his affection and thought are theirs. Thus are Spirits conjoined with man, through whom he is ruled by the Lord.
A Spirit with a corporeal sphere. (See Speak.)
Spirits act more subtly than men. Explained.
These Spirits correspond to the corruptions of the purer blood... Described.
The things which come forth with the Spirits and Angels with a man are perceived by the man just as if they were in himself. Explained.
The presence of Spirits with man is according to his loves. Explained... Thus everyone may know the quality of the Spirits with him, provided he observes that of his loves, or ends.
The Spirits of the general voluntary sense. Fully described. (See General.)
An intermediate Spirit.
Spirits of this Earth relate to the external man. (See Society.)
Spirits from this Earth (infested) the Spirits who relate to the internal sensuous. Described.
The external sensuous Spirits (could not breathe in the sphere) of the internal sensuous ones. Described, Explained.

The corporeal things are the most general of those which belong to the spirit; (and) exist and subsist from the things of the spirit: thus the things of the spirit are relatively particular. (This is made evident when the man becomes a Spirit); and, when the same Spirit becomes an Angel, ... the things he had previously seen and felt in general... he sees and feels in particular. Explained, Signified.
That man is a Spirit, and is clothed with a body. Explained.
His Spirit is himself...
(Spirits are Known by their situation relatively to the human body. See Situation at AC 3639.)
Spirits seen near me are mostly Subjects of entire Societies. (See Subject.)
(Ten classes of Spirits, and their correspondence with various parts of the body. Enumerated.)
For man's spirit is in the light of Heaven; his body in that of the world.
It is the Spirit which lives in the body, and thinks.
For man's spirit is in society with Spirits and Angels, (and so the man knows this truth).
Spirits (are Known) from the light in which they are. Explained.
(A conversation with Spirits about life.)
The withdrawal of delight is effected (there) by the separation of the Spirits in whose society they are. (The effect of this.)
Not knowing that the life of their body is from that of their spirit...
That the soul or spirit is the man who lives after death...
They marvelled that Spirits have eyes...
Spirits appear to themselves exactly like men, see each other, hear, speak, feel their members by the touch, more exquisitely than (when here). Explained. AC 4622:2, Explained.
Man can see Spirits only with the eyes of his spirit; he sees them when the Lord opens his internal sight, as was done with the prophets...
(The representatives) affected the Spirits who were with (the Israelites)...
This combat arises among the Spirits who are with the man. Explained.
The Divine truth is the Spirit of Truth. Illustrated.
For all things there are adapted to the sensations of Spirits and Angels...
(How men might easily come into right ideas about the Spirit. Explained.)

It is not the body which sees, etc. but its spirit; and therefore when the spirit puts off the body, it is in its own sensations, in those in which it had been in the body, and indeed in much more exquisite ones. Explained, Described.

As soon (after death) as a man observes that he has more exquisite sensations, especially when he begins to speak with other Spirits, he notices that he is in the other life, and that the death of his body had been the continuation of the life of his spirit. (Two examples of this.)
The sensitive life of spirits is twofold, real, and not real. Explained... Whatever comes from the proprium of a Spirit is not real. Explained.
Beware when you come into the other life; for evil Spirits present illusions, and if they cannot deceive, they try to persuade thereby that nothing is real...
The correspondence between... the things of the spirit which is within man, and those of the body. (Explained under Speak, here.)
(The Spirits of the ears. Fully quoted under Ear.) AC 4653. a. AC 4654. AC 4655. AC 4656. AC 4657. AC 4658.
For the spirit of man is among the Spirits who are in the other life, and thinks there...
a. Substantiated things which are nearer the spirit, and which at last are in the spirit.
Aristotle had followed obediently the things which his spirit had dictated.

A woman often appeared to Aristotle, who stroked his cheek with her beautiful hand. Such women were sometimes seen by the ancients, who called them Pallases, and the one who appeared to him was from the Spirits who as men in ancient times had been delighted with ideas...

It might be supposed that the spirit dwells within the body, and that the body as it were clothes it; but it is to be known that the spirit of man is in the body, in the whole, and in every part of it; and that it is its purer substance, in both its motory and its sensory organs, and everywhere else; and that the body is what is material everywhere annexed to it... This is what is meant by man being a Spirit, and the body serving him for uses in the world; and by the spirit being the internal of man, and the body his external. From this it is evident that after death man is in similar active and sensitive life: and is also in the human form, as (here), but in a more perfect one.

For the internal man, or spirit of man, knows not what old age is; but, as the body, or external man, grows old, the former passes into newness of life: the spirit of man is perfected in age as his Corporeal decreases, and still more so in the other life...

Although the spirit knows not what old age is, (and) the spirit is what thinks in the body, and the body has life from it; (yet) this thought of the spirit cannot be communicated to the body, and so cause man to know that he lives after death, for the reason that so long as the spirit remains in the body, it cannot think otherwise than from the principles which the natural man has imbued...
I will pour My Spirit upon them () = to instruct about truths.
The unclean Spirit () = the uncleanness of life with man; and also the unclean Spirits who are with him; for unclean Spirits dwell in the uncleanness of man's life.
How Spirits and Angels are nourished. (See Food.)

No Spirit or Angel is permitted to inflow into man's taste. (Explained under Taste.) Yet there are wandering infernal Spirits... who study to do so, and (thus) possess the man's interiors. At this day very many are possessed by them; for there are interior obsessions now. (The signs of them.)
These pernicious Spirits try to loosen all internal bonds. Explained. When these have been loosed, the man is obsessed by such Spirits. (Continued. See Obsess.)

How these Spirits are driven away. When they supposed that they were penetrating to the interiors of the head, they were conveyed away through excrementitious ways... They correspond to the filthy cavernules where the itch is.
A Spirit... has all the sensations he had while (here), except taste: in place of this he has something analogous which is adjoined to smell. Explained.
To what province they are allotted is hidden from Spirits; but not from Angels.
(The Societies of friendship) turn the Spirits who are with others to themselves, and thus transfer the delight of the other to themselves.
It appears to Spirits and Angels that they too move from place to place. Explained.
Every Spirit and Angel sees the good to the right, and the evil to the left. Explained.
(A Spirit from another Earth who ardently desired to be admitted into Heaven. Described.) AC 8847.
(Some Spirits who had hated me when in the body. Described.)

Man rises immediately after death, and then appears to himself in a body exactly as in the world, with the same kind of a face, members, arms, hands, feet, breast, belly, loins; and, when he sets and touches himself, he says he is a man just as in the world; yet it is not his external... which he sees and touches, but his internal, which constitutes that very human itself which is alive. Explained... That I might be certain of these things, it has been granted; me to touch Spirits themselves, and to speak with them often about this subject. AC 5078:5, Explained.
A rational natural man comprehends that there are Spirits and Angels who are invisible: but a sensuous man does not comprehend it.
When man is in interior thought from affection... he is almost in his Spirit... But when he is in pleasures... his life is in the body...
By water and the Spirit = by faith and charity.
The faces of Spirits and Angels are formed from the exterior Natural.
The Spirits of the thymus gland. Described.
The first agitations of Spirits. Representation.
The Genii and Spirits of the receptacle and ducts of the chyle. Described.
The provinces of Spirits and Angels as known from the gyres. Example(s).
The Spirits of the gall bladder. Described.
The Spirits of the sores called tubercles. Described.
In the degree of such clearness or obscurity (of truths), Spirits are awake or asleep.

His spirit was troubled () = disturbance... The spirit, here, and elsewhere, means the interior affection and thought, which in fact are the spirit of man. The ancients called these the spirit; lint by the spirit, in special, they meant the interior man who will live after death.
But by the spirit, at this day, when read of in such a sense, is meant the mere thinking principle, without any other subject than the body. Example(s).
Therefore many of the magi communicated with Spirits...
Hence Angels and Spirits can meet, all whom they ever heard of.
When man is being tempted, unclean Spirits are near him. Explained.
The hair of Spirits. Described.
The garments of Spirits and Angels. (See Garment.)

The Spirit of God () = good from the interior, thus from the Divine; for the Spirit of God is that which proceeds from the Divine, thus from good itself... and that which proceeds from it is truth in which is good; and this is what is signified in the Word by the Spirit of God. The Spirit itself does not proceed, but the truth in which is good... the Spirit being the instrumental through which it is produced.
In that state (of humiliation) there is a deficiency of the spirits...
To be born of the spirit = the good of life.
(The Spirits of the peritoneum infested by those of the kidneys, ureters, and bladder. Described.) See also AC 5379.
The Spirits of the kidneys, ureters, and bladder. Described. AC 5381. AC 5382. AC 5383. AC 5384.

As soon as any Spirit comes to another, and still more to a man, he at once knows his thoughts and affections, and all he had done, thus all his present state... But some Spirits perceive the interior things, and some only the exterior ones...
The over-conscientious Spirits and their correspondence. Described.
A piratical Spirit of the urine. Described. (See also AC 5388.)
The Spirits who correspond to the voiding of the urine.
The wandering Spirits of the neck of the bladder. Described.
A disorderly crowd of Spirits reduced into order. (See Choir.)
Mediate Spirits and their use. Explained.
With every man, there are two Spirits from Hell and two Angels from Heaven; (otherwise) man (as now born) could not live. (Continued. See Angel.)
The Spirits of the skins and integuments. Described. AC 5554. AC 5555. AC 5556.
(Female Spirits through whom others speak. Described under Speak, and at AC 5561.)
Spirits who say it is so, experimentally. Explained.
The Spirits of the cartilages and bones. Described. AC 5561-5564.
The Spirits of the teeth. Described. AC 5566-5568.
Spirits as characterised by the hair. Described.
The like happens with Spirits who are being initiated into good through truths.
The Spirits of diseases. General article.
Spirits who infuse unclean colds... The same induce things which disturb the mind. They also induce swoons.
How Spirits destroyed whole armies. Explained. SE 1783.
Spirits who excite enmities among others in order to dominate. Described.
The Spirits who despise the Word... are kept separate from others... and communicate only with those of the same character.

Spirits who had been hypocrites. Described... When applied to man they induce great tedium. Described... They want to be called devils, provided they are allowed to command the Hells. Explained... They are afterwards rejected out of the World of Spirits.

Spirits with me who induced an unendurable oppression in the stomach... When they were removed, it at once ceased. Such Spirits are those who (here) had lived in filthy idleness. Described... The sphere of such with the sick induces a torpor on the members and joints.
On the Angels and Spirits with man. General article. AC 5976, continued.
No man, Spirit, or Angel has life from himself, thus cannot think and will from himself. Explained.
In order that the Lord's life may inflow... there are Angels and Spirits continually with man... two of each. Explained.
The two Spirits adjoined to a man cause communication with Hell, and the two Angels, with Heaven... If these communications were taken away, the man would fall down dead. (Shown by experiment.)
Few believe there is any Spirit with them, or that there are any Spirits. (The cause of this.)

As men are not in order... there is particular influx into them, that is, there are Angels and Spirits with them, through whom there is influx. (Otherwise) men would rush into every wickedness. Explained.
The Spirits with a man are changed according to his state. Explained.
The Spirits with a man are such as he himself is: there are avaricious Spirits with a miser, and so on... Man summons Spirits from Hell according to his life.
While evil Spirits are with a man, they are in the World of Spirits. (See Evil Spirit.)
The Spirits who flow to a man enter into all his memory. (Fully quoted under Memory.) AC 5857. AC 5858. AC 5859. AC 5865:2. AC 6192. AC 6200.
Spirits inflow into the thoughts and voluntary things of man; but Angels into the ends. Explained.
Before it was opened to me to speak with Spirits, I supposed that no Spirit or Angel could know my thoughts...
A Spirit knows not only the thoughts which the man himself knows, but also the least things of his thoughts and affections, which the man does not know... AC 6214:2.
The Spirits and Angels who are with a man are (Subjects). Explained. AC 5983.
Spirits are learned with the learned, stupid with the stupid, etc.
Whatever Spirits think or speak from the man's memory, they suppose to be their own. Described... They have their own scientifics as well, but are not allowed to use them.
Spirits who supposed they had always been with me. Described.

The Spirits with a man put on his persuasions also... Thus the Spirits with those who are in heresies are in the like, and so on. This is in order that man may... not be disturbed by anything proper to the Spirit.

Thus man... as to his Spirit is in consort with other Spirits, and is so joined to them that he cannot think or will anything, except together with them... Thus only can he be led by the Lord. (Continued. See Society.)
The Spirits with man do not know they are with him; only the Angels know this; for they are adjoined to his soul or spirit, and not to his body. (Continued. See Speak.)
With me, however, Spirits have known that I was a man in the body, and (they could) see through my eyes, and hoar those speaking to me.
If evil Spirits were to perceive that they are... separate Spirits from the man... they would try to destroy him. (Continued. See Evil Spirit.)
As evil Spirits have heard that there are Spirits with man, they have supposed they could meet those Spirits, and man together with them... but in vain.
A Spirit, not evil, was permitted to pass to a certain man... He said that there appeared to him a black inanimate something. Explained.
An evil Spirit was let into the state of the body. Explained.
Usually Spirits are not allowed to look into the corporeals of man... When Spirits look into the things of the light of the world, they appear to them as mere darkness.
When a man becomes a Spirit he is not allowed to use his scientifics, and yet he thinks and speaks about truth and good much more distinctly and perfectly.

When man dies... the Internal which lives after the separation from the external, is what is then called a Spirit, but it is the man himself who had lived in the body, and he appears to himself and others as a man... endowed with the same faculties... and, when he does not reflect... he supposes that he is in his body in the world. AC 6054, Described.
The breath... relates to the things of the understanding.
Sadness of the spirit, or understanding. Signified, Explained.
Fibres from the brain full of spirit.
Truths clothe good, as... fibres the spirit.
Morning, noon, and evening with Spirits and Explained.
The spirit of Jacob revived () = new life.

The reason there are two Spirits and Angels with every man, is that there are two kinds of Spirits in Hell, and two kinds of Angels in Heaven... The first kind of Spirits are called simply Spirits, and act into intellectual things; the second kind are called Genii, and act into voluntary things. Explained. (Continued. See Genii.)
The Spirits were very indignant at this experience; for every one of them wants to think and speak from himself.

At this day there are very many Spirits who want to inflow not only into man's thoughts and affections, but also into his speech and actions, thus also into his corporeals; when yet these are exempt from the particular influx of Spirits and Angels, and are ruled by general influx. Explained... The Spirits who want this are such as had been adulterers. Explained... Such are not allowed to go into the World of Spirits. Hence there are no external obsessions now; but there are internal ones. Explained.
Spirits who are to be called corporeal, seen. They appeared as if in a gross body. Who they had been (here).
The breath of his lips () = Divine truth from which is Judgment.
These things are known even to simple Spirits.

For many years all my thoughts and affections... have inflowed through Spirits and Angels as media, as I have perceived evidently. Described. (This shows how man is ruled through them.) AC 6197, Described.

When Spirits come to a man they put on all his memory... The Spirits suppose these things to be their own. Thus they act with the man as if they were the man. But they are not allowed to enter farther with the man than to the things of his thought and will, and not to those of his actions and speech... They do not know that they are with a man. Explained. AC 6193. Explained.

I have sometimes thought and spoken without reflecting that Spirits were present; but they at once addressed me, and told me that they did not know it was not they who were thinking. The nearest Spirits believed it was themselves altogether; the more remote ones less so; and those still more remote, still less so.

Spirits have long been with me, neither very good, nor very evil, who could inflow inwardly into the affections... and they so bound themselves to me that it seemed as if they could scarcely be separated. Described. (This shows that it is loves which conjoin.)

Spirits are associated to a man according to his loves... As soon as I have begun to love anything intensely, Spirits were present who were in such love, and they were not removed until the love had ceased.

Spirits have been with me who supposed it was they who lived... thus that they were I; and when they were told that they were separate Spirits, and that I too was a Spirit as to the interiors, they could not believe it. Described. AC 6199.
As for nine years I have continually been in consort with Spirits and Angels, I have carefully observed how the case is with influx. Explained.
The Spirits who were in a more subtle sphere...

When I have thought about a man known to me... that whole man, as he existed in my thought and affection, appeared in a moment with the Spirits. So when I have thought of any city... the Spirits knew in a moment everything I had seen or known about it. It is the same with matters of knowledge. (Explained.)

Thus did my thought appear with Spirits when I was a little withdrawn from sensuous things; but (not) when my thought was in sensuous things... To the sensuous are adjoined like Spirits; and these Spirits apprehend scarcely any more things with a man than those which come to his sensation; for they are grosser than the rest.

When I have been let down into what is sensuous... the Spirits who are in that grosser sphere infused shocking and scandalous things... At this day such Spirits abound... and the influx from them with man causes him to be self-indulgent, and live for himself and the world... To be elevated from them, man must think about eternal life.

There is another influx, which is not through the Spirits with the man, but through others sent from some infernal Society into the sphere of the man's life; and these speak among themselves about such things as are adverse to the man, (causing him to feel sad, etc. See Speak.)
Such Spirits have often been with me. (Fully described.)
See Tempt.
Why speech and action are not ruled through particular Spirits, as thought and will are. (Explained under Speak, here.)
Spirits are allotted to every member of speech and of action; but these Spirits are not aware of it.
(The prophets then spoke and acted) from the Spirits who occupied their bodies. Described. I was shown how they were acted upon by the Spirits. Described.

The Spirits occupied their bodies, insomuch that there was scarcely anything left except that they knew they existed. There were certain Spirits for this use, who did not want to obsess men, but merely to enter into the corporeal affections of the man, (and thus) into all things of his body. The Spirits usually with me said that I was absent from them while in that state.
The Spirits who possessed my body... afterwards told me that they had (supposed) they had life as in the body.

How difficult it is for man to believe that Spirits know his thoughts... Before I spoke with Spirits, it happened that a certain Spirit said a few words to me about what I was thinking of. I was astounded... Then, when I began to speak with Spirits, I was indignant that I could think nothing which they did not know of... but the use of a few days made it familiar to me.
When Spirits have inquired anything from me, they have received an answer by merely looking into my thought.

(Ideas of the learned about Spirits.) They could not be brought to believe that Spirits enjoy any sense; and everything else they had thought about Spirits was devoid of all quality. The reason was that they had placed life in the body. Explained... But the unlearned, who have been in the good of faith, are not such...

Before the Spirits with a man, objects do not appear as the man sees them with his eyes, nor are words apprehended as the man hears them with his ears; but [they appear and are apprehended] as the man thinks [of them]. Explained.
There are malignant Spirits who have devised arts to prevent (in part) the angelic influx. Described.
It is the sense of the spirit which sensates through the external sense... AC 6948:3.
I have seen Spirits separated from an angelic Society because they believed... in physical influx.
Spirits who reason much, perceive little of what is true and good. Described.
When such think about the spirit or soul, they can have no idea of it than as of the invisible things in nature... some as of a mere thinking principle...
That good... may protect Spirits who have recently come from the world... it acts through truth.
Every spirit thinks and speaks from others; and these others from others; and so on. AC 6471, Example(s).
Spirits who continually injected doubts. Explained.
I have often spoken with Spirits about fortune... Accidents happen because such Spirits are present. Explained. AC 6494. SE 4562.
They who think exteriorly... communicate solely with the grosser Spirits; but they who think interiorly... with the Angels. (The difference explained.)
How angelic ideas inflow into those of Spirits. (See Idea.) AC 6615.
Certain Spirits gloried [in the idea] that they know all things. These Spirits relate to the memory. Explained. (See AC 6696. AC 6808.)
Spirits who deny that there is anything interior in the Word.
Ideas of thought are the words of Spirits; and ideas of still more interior thought are the words of Angels.
Spirits and Angels think and speak abstractedly. Explained.
Spirits in like evils and falsities are present.
The Spirits of Mercury. Treated of. AC 6807, General article. AC 6921, continued. AC 7069, continued.
Spirits and Angels from other Earths are all separate from each other according to the Earths. Explained... Nor are they consociated in the Heavens, except in the Third.
Spirits can search the memory with the utmost skill. AC 6811.
In Mercury many men speak with Spirits, and hence possess Knowledges of spiritual Things...
The memory of Spirits is much more perfect than that of men. Explained. AC 6931.
In order that (evil men may be kept in the simulation of what is honourable and just) Spirits who are in simple good are joined to them...

The Spirits of our Earth, especially when recently in the other life, love corporeal and worldly things... and desire to know such things there. They are therefore... kept in the Lower Earth until they are averse to such things; and are then elevated into Heaven.
A Spirit can utter in a moment things which a man can scarcely utter in half an hour. (Fully quoted under Speak.)
(The speech of Spirits is unintelligible to man; and that of Angels is unintelligible to Spirits. Fully quoted under Speak.)
For the Word which is uttered by a Spirit or Angel proceeds from His Divine Human.
The prophets wrote as the Spirits dictated from the Divine...
All Spirits whatever have been men... and the Spirits themselves are exactly such as they had been while they lived in the world.

The Spirits of other Earths do not appear within the sphere in which are the Spirits of our Earth, but outside it, some at a greater, and some at a lesser distance, and towards different quarters. Explained. AC 7358, Explained. AC 7800.
Directors = intermediate Spirits.
(Our) sun does not appear to any Spirit, nor anything of its light; it is thick darkness to them. (Continued. See Sun.)
Positions of the planets in the ideas of Spirits and Angels. AC 7247. AC 7800.
Spirits appear near their own planet, but outside of it.
Spirits of our Earth speaking with those of Mercury. Described.
Straitness of spirit () = a state near despair. Explained.
To the merely natural such appear weak and sick in spirit, but they are strong; whereas the merely natural... are quite weak as to the spirit, because they are spiritually dead.
(The times of the day with Spirits. Explained.)
The Spirits of Venus. General article.
The Spirits of Mars. General article. AC 7475, continued. AC 7620, continued.
The speech of the Spirits of Mars. (Fully quoted under Speak, and at AC 7745. AC 7747.)
The respiration of the Spirits of Mars. Described.

The Spirits of Mars appear to themselves as men such as they had been in the world, and therefore they appear in the same way to others; for everyone there appears to others as he appears to himself, because the perception is communicated... They had known they were Spirits clothed with a body, and had thought chiefly about the life of their spirit in their body. (Continued. See Mars.)
All Spirits are in the human form; but not in so prominent a one as that in which are the Spirits of Mars.
The Spirits of Mars are among the best of all Spirits from our solar system...
In the sphere of the Spirits of Mars the Spirits of our Earth became as if insane. Explained. (See also AC 9108.)
For the spirit, regarded in itself, is the affection in form...
The Spirits of Jupiter. General article. AC 8021, continued. AC 8242. AC 8371.
There are many kinds of Spirits from Jupiter. Three kinds of them described.
In (Jupiter) Spirits speak with the inhabitants, and instruct them, and also chastise them. The reason Spirits speak with them is that they think much about... the life after death...
To speak with Spirits and Angels was also common on this Earth in ancient times, from a like cause... but this living communication with Heaven was closed as man became external. Explained.
The speech of Spirits with the inhabitants of Jupiter. Explained.
The chastising Spirits of Jupiter, described. AC 8021, Described. AC 8027.
The instructing Spirits of Jupiter, Described. AC 7806.
The angelic Spirits of Jupiter, described. AC 7807. AC 7808.
When the face in the window was seen the Spirit instantly departed.

The men of Jupiter are not allowed to speak back to the Spirits; nor to mention to anyone that a Spirit has spoken to them... These Spirits of Jupiter, when with me, at first supposed they were with a man of their earth... AC 8385.
When Angels are about to come, a Spirit is sent before who prepares the way. Explained.
When Spirits of Jupiter become Angels there appear horses as of fire...
The Spirits of Jupiter are altogether unwilling to be in the company of Spirits of our Earth. Explained. AC 8115.
I will pour My spirit () = the good of charity.
The temptations of Spirits. Described.
Spirit () = what is alive.
(Such inhabitants of Jupiter) are deprived of respiration, and thence of life, by Spirits...
A Spirit from the Lower Earth came to me. Described.

The Spirits and Angels of Jupiter relate to the Imaginative of thought, and thus to an active state of the interior parts; whereas the Spirits of our Earth relate to various functions of the exterior parts of the body; and the Imaginative of thought cannot inflow into these functions while they want to dominate...
(The speech of the Spirits of Jupiter fully described under Speak, here.)
Thus the mere externals of the Israelites could communicate with Spirits, and through them with Angels. AC 10602:end.
(A Spirit of Jupiter who had a very tender conscience. Described.)
Such Spirits and Angels are with a man as is his universal Regnant. Explained.
As there is nothing of spiritual life in such, it is said there is no breath in them ().
By the unclean Spirit, when he went out, is meant the acknowledgement and belief of truth... By his return with seven others, a state of profanation. NJHD 172:2. Explained.
The soul or spirit of man is in Heaven, and his body in the world...
The Spirits of Saturn. General article. AC 9104, continued.
The inhabitants of Saturn, when they come of age, speak with Spirits, by whom they are instructed about the Lord... and how to live.
When any want to seduce the Spirits of Saturn... they say they want to die... Spirits of our Earth sometimes deride them...

The inhabitants and Spirits of Saturn relate to the intermediate between the spiritual and the natural sense, acceding to the spiritual... Hence these Spirits often seem to themselves to be rapt into Heaven, and afterwards let back... AC 9107.
Some Spirits of this Earth passed over to the Spirits of Saturn, who... appear at the end of our solar world. (The conversation between them. AC 9105.)
The Spirits of Saturn then spoke with me through intermediate Spirits...
The Spirits of Saturn are visited by those of Mercury. Described.
The Spirits of our Earth relate to the natural and corporeal sense; thus to the external man; but the Spirits of Saturn to the internal man...
When Angels converse about two discrepant truths, two disputing Spirits are presented below who are the Subjects of many Societies...
For when an Angel or Spirit is in externals, he is in shade; but when in internals he is in the delights of heavenly loves...
The Spirits of the moon. General article.
The simpler Spirits with me laughed at them. Explained.
Spirits and Angels often speak to the inhabitants of the moon...
That the world cannot receive the Spirit of Truth, because it does not see him, nor know him = that it will not acknowledge the Lord with faith of heart, because external things will obscure.

As respiration corresponds to the life of faith, (the latter) is called breath; as in [the expression] drawing the breath and letting out the breath; and hence too, Spirits, in Hebrew, are so called from wind, and in the Word are compared to wind. Illustrated. AC 9818:15.
Hence Spirits and Angels are forms of their own use... Hence too it is that the quality of Spirits is Known as soon as they are present. Explained.
To be born of water and the spirit = through truths of faith and the good of love. AC 9454:end. (Compare AC 9818:11. AC 10237. a.[end]. AC 10388.)
In every other Earth truth Divine is manifested orally through Spirits and Angels... But this is done within the families, (and therefore a new revelation is constantly necessary).
At this day Heaven is closed; for scarcely anyone speaks with Angels and Spirits. (Continued. See Speak.)
How far Moses was admitted into Heaven, was shown me representatively by means of a Spirit. Described.
On the men, Spirits, and Angels of the Earths in the starry heaven. General article. (See Speak.)
(Why so few are now allowed to speak with Spirits and Angels. Fully explained under Speak, here.)

Through changes of state, Angels and Spirits can be translated from one place to another; from one Earth into another; and even to Earths at the end of the universe. In like manner a man as to his spirit... AC 10734.
Spirits who are in the First Heaven.
There are always Spirits and Angels with man... Through them man is connected with the Lord; and thus subsists the human race and also Heaven.
The Spirits of (the First Earth). AC 9693, General article. AC 9793.
For Spirits remain near their own Earth. AC 9968, Explained.
In that gulf appeared very many men, who were Spirits... These were guards, to prevent Spirits from this system from passing, without permission, into any other.
Spirits, in the Word, = the life of the intellectual part; heart, that of the voluntary part. AC 9818:3. Illustrated.
Filled with the spirit of wisdom () = with Divine truth. Explained.

Spirit often occurs in the Word, and, when man is treated of, by his spirit is signified the good and truth inscribed on the intellectual part, consequently, the life of this; (for) man, as to his interiors, is a Spirit, and as to them is together with Spirits. AC 9818:3, Explained, Illustrated.

Hence by Spirit, when the Lord is treated of, is meant the Divine truth proceeding from His Divine good; and this, when... received by man, is the Spirit of Truth, the Spirit of God, and the Holy Spirit... AC 9818:13, Illustrated.
That spirit, in a general sense, = the life of man's respiration. Illustrated.
Thus spirit = the life of man. That, in special, it = the life of truth, which is the life of the intellectual part, and is called intelligence. Illustrated.
The Spirit, here, = intelligence and wisdom.
The life from Divine truths is Spirit.

The Divine truth, consequently the Divine wisdom and intelligence, are called the Spirit of Jehovah; here, the spirit of wisdom and intelligence, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Jehovah (). Further Illustrated AC 9857:4. AC 10196:2, Explained. AC 10570:7.
That the Spirit of Jehovah = the Divine truth, and the derivative heavenly life for the man who receives it. Illustrated.
Spirit of judgment = Divine truth. ( = wisdom from Divine truth. AC 9857:3.)
Spirit of holiness = the Lord as to Divine truth, thus the Divine truth which is from the Lord.
To make angels spirits () = receptions of Divine truth.
When intelligence and wisdom are taken away from Spirits, which happens when the angelic Societies are removed from them, their head covering appears to be taken away, and they then become stupid...
All Spirits and Angels appear clothed in garments according to their state of truth.
The breath of the nostrils = the heavenly life itself which is from the Lord.
The Spirits of the Second Earth. General article.
The breath of His mouth () = the life from Divine truth.

The spirit breatheth where it listeth, and thou hearest the voice thereof, but knowest not whence it Cometh and whither it goeth; so is everyone who is born of the spirit (): the spirit = the life of charity through faith. ( = the Divine truth which inflows from the Lord through the internal of man into his externa, whence the regenerating man has the life of faith. AC 10240.)
The Spirit of truth () = the Divine truth proceeding from the Lord. AC 10151:4.
(The spirit is not continuous with the body.)
Around Spirits who are in truths from good appear most beautiful representatives. Described... But around those in truths (only), appear rocks, marshes, etc.
Unless Spirits and Angels were with man, through whom the influx is effected, he could not live a moment... AC 10483:2.
With Spirits below the Heavens, there are riches according to their reception of truth and good from the Lord.
Spirits and Angels think by spiritual ideas, and also speak by them...
Spirit is opposed to flesh, because by Spirit is signified life from the Lord; and by flesh, life from man. Illustrated.
Among Spirits are very many who imitate Divine things...
Spirits are nothing but their own truths and goods which they had put on in the world; and yet are human forms...
The Spirits of the Third Earth, Described. AC 10378. AC 10384.
They could not be with the Spirits of our Earth. AC 10312. Explained. AC 10381. AC 10517, Explained. AC 10710.
For Spirits are consociated and dissociated according to the affections and the derivative thoughts. AC 10585:end.
Therefore the Spirits of that Earth do not appear in a well-defined human form; but as clouds. Described.
I have filled him with the spirit of God () = influx and illustration from the Divine truth which is from the Lord's good.
These Spirits keep themselves at a distance, because their correspondence is... with man's interior things.
(I told him) that what he reprehended was not mine, but belonged to the Spirits around me; for what I think I do not think from myself, but from them, by influx.
As there is nothing Divine in them, it is said there is no breath in them ().
Spirits turn themselves according to their loves. Explained.

Spirits go nowhere else than to those with whom they are consociated by love; hence the quality of Spirits as to truth is known from the ways and streets in which they go; for all truth leads to its own love.
The Spirits of the Fourth Earth. Described. AC 10710.
I was not conveyed to the Fourth Earth; but the Spirits of it were brought to me.
How Spirits of quite another genius may be associated with Spirits with whom there is to be conjunction. Explained.

The External (of man) which is accommodated to uses in the other life together with the internal (of man) is called a Spirit; a good Spirit and Angel if the man had been good; and an evil Spirit if he had been evil.
The spirit of man appears (there) in a human form exactly as (here). (His faculties enumerated.)
These ideas are of man's spirit... and he comes into them when he becomes a Spirit, and by them converses with other Spirits.
Those who think in their spirit abstractedly from their body...
As to his spirit, man is in society with Spirits, and, as to his interior thought... with Angels. Hence man has the faculty of thinking.
Angels and Spirits... have faces, arms, hands, feet... dwellings; and live together exactly as do men, upon an earth. Described.
A Spirit with me who had been a very pathetic preacher. Described. AC 10736.
The Spirits of the Fifth Earth. Described. AC 10751.
Spirits from our Earth visit them. Described.
All Spirits know about their own Earth, when their natural memory is opened...

The Spirits said that when leave is given they appear to the inhabitants of their Earth, and speak with them as men; which is effected by their being let into their natural memory... and the inhabitants suppose them to be men (until) they vanish. Illustrated. This rarely happens now on our Earth, lest men should be compelled to believe...
The preacher took hold of the hand of a woman on that Earth; but, as she perceived that he was a Spirit... she hastened away.

Every man is a Spirit as to his interiors, and it is that which lives in the body... and it is the spirit of everyone from which he has the human form, consequently which is principally the man, and in a like form... visible (only) before the eyes of Spirits...
On my asking Spirits... whether they wanted to be reclothed with their earthly body, they fled far away...
Many Spirits and Angels from our Earth accompanied me (to the Sixth Earth).
Only in two places (on the way) did I see Spirits...
The Spirits of the Sixth Earth. Described. AC 10808, General article. AC 10833.
The spiritual Sun appears only to the Angels, and not to the Spirits who are below. Explained.
Monkish Spirits seen with a crowd of Spirits of the Sixth Earth, mostly evil. Described.
For Spirits and Angels dwell in the same way as they had done (here). Explained.
Spirits and Angels... can see the things in the world through the eyes of a man to whom the Lord grants to speak with Spirits and Angels...

Upright Spirits... grieved at the ignorance within the Church about Spirits and Angels; and indignantly told me to relate that they are not minds without form, nor ethereal spirits; but in form are men; and that they see, hear, and feel as well as those who are in the world. HH 456, Explained.
The pulmonary breath = the understanding, and the truth of faith.

The spirit... in some who were beautiful in face (was seen to be) deformed, black, and monstrous... But in some who were not beautiful, it was lovely, fair, and angelic. And the spirit of a man appears after death such as it had been in the body.
The interiors make the face of an Angel and a Spirit.
Man, too, as to his spirit, turns in the same way. Explained.
A Spirit who believed that he thought from himself. Described.

When an Angel or Spirit comes to a man, and, by conversion to him, is conjoined with him, he comes into all his memory, insomuch that he scarcely knows but that he knows from himself all the man knows...
At this day there is no longer such conjunction with Angels, but with Spirits not in Heaven.
Spirits will not believe it is the man who speaks, but they in him; (and) that all the man knows is from them...

Another reason why Angels and Spirits conjoin themselves so closely with man that they suppose the man's things to be their own, is that there is such a conjunction between the spiritual and the natural world with man that they are as it were one. But, as man had separated himself from Heaven, it was provided... that there should be Angels and Spirits with every man, and that he should be ruled by the Lord through them. This is the reason for so close a conjunction. Otherwise, man could have been ruled through the general influx from Heaven without having Spirits and Angels adjoined to him. HH 296, Explained.
To speak with Spirits is rarely granted (now), because it is dangerous; for the Spirits then know they are with a man... References.

Some who lead a solitary life sometimes hear Spirits... without danger; but the Spirits with them are removed... at intervals, to prevent their knowing they are with a man. For most Spirits do not know there is any other world... and therefore the man is not allowed to speak back to them, otherwise they would know.

They who think much about religious things, (so as) to see them in themselves, begin to hear Spirits speaking to them. Explained... But such are visionaries and enthusiasts, and whatever Spirit they bear they believe to be the Holy Spirit, when yet they are enthusiastic ones. Such Spirits see falsities as truths... and therefore they persuade those with whom they inflow. As these Spirits began to persuade evils also... they have been removed by degrees. (Continued. See Enthusiasm.)
Rarely, since those times, has anyone spoken with Angels... but some with Spirits. Explained.
The Lord spoke the Word to the prophets through Spirits, whom He filled with His aspect. Explained.

A Spirit filled with the Divine... knows not but that he is the Lord, and that what he speaks is Divine... Afterwards, he perceives he is a Spirit... Such was the state of the Spirits who spoke to the prophets... The Spirits believed themselves to be Jehovah. SE 1957.
No Angel or Spirit is allowed to speak to a man from his own memory. (Fully quoted under Memory.)

There are Spirits, called natural and corporeal Spirits, who, when they come to man, do not conjoin themselves with his thought, like other Spirits, but enter into his body, and take possession of all his senses, speak through his mouth, and act through his members, supposing, then, that all things of the man are theirs. These are the Spirits who obsess man; but they have been cast into Hell, and quite removed...
(The good and evil Spirits with man). Fully explained. See Evil Spirit. HH 293. HH 295.
All Spirits in the World of Spirits have communication with Heaven or with Hell. (Continued. See Society.)

The Spirits with man are changed according to the changes of his affections: hence some Spirits are with him in infancy; others in childhood; others in adolescence and young manhood, and others in old age. (These four classes of Spirits, and the Heavens with which they communicate. Described, Enumerated.)
As to his speech and actions, man is ruled through general influx, and therefore the Spirits adjoined to him have nothing in common with these.
The influx through Spirits is called mediate.
The Spirits with man (whether good or evil) never inflow from their own memory and derivative thought... Still, through them there inflows with man, good or evil affection. (Continued. See Influx.)

Spirits not yet in conjunction with Hell (who) love undigested things... are present where there are such things in a man, and speak there together from their evil affection; and if this affection is contrary to the man's, it becomes in him sadness and melancholy anxiety; but if it is in agreement, it becomes in him gladness and cheerfulness. These Spirits appear near the stomach. Described.
Yet man cannot think one whit without Spirits adjoined to him; and his spiritual life depends upon it.
It is the spirit which thinks in the body. HH 432.

For the spirit of man is altogether such as is his love; moreover, the body of every Spirit and Angel is the external form of his love exactly corresponding to the internal form which is that of his mind... HH 527:2.
And that which is in the spirit of a man when he leaves the body remains after death; for he then lives a Spirit man.

Certain Spirits, not evil, fell as it were into sleep, and were translated, as to their interiors... into Heaven; (which) can be done with Spirits before their interiors have been opened. (What they saw, described.)
When, with a Spirit man, good has been conjoined with truth, he comes into Heaven... But when, with a Spirit man, evil has been conjoined with falsity, he comes into Hell.
When Spirits are mentioned, those who are in the World of Spirits are meant...
Every man is a Spirit as to his interiors. General article. HH 436. HH 437.
(Thus) whatever lives with man is his spirit. HH 433.

It follows that the spirit is the man himself; or, that man, regarded in himself, is a Spirit, and is in a like form; for whatever lives and feels in man is of his spirit, and everything in man... lives and feels; and therefore when the body is separated from its spirit... the man remains a man, and is alive. Some think even in their cold body, while it is lying on the bier. HH 453, Explained.

(Thus) the spirit of man is equally in a form... and equally enjoys sensories and senses when separated from the body; and everything... of the life of sense which man has, is not of his body, but of his spirit... Hence Spirits, equally with men, see, hear, and feel... The spirit sensates naturally while in the body, through what is material added to it; yet it sensates spiritually at the same time, by thinking and willing.
(Thus) man, regarded in himself, is a spirit; and the Corporeal which is added to him... is not the man; but is only the Instrumental of his spirit. (The Spiritual which beasts have. Explained.)
Every man, even while in the body, is as to his spirit in society with Spirits. Explained.
Being carried by the spirit into another place. Explained.

The inmost communication of the spirit is with the respiration and with the motion of the heart; its thought, with (the former), and its affection with (the latter); and therefore when these two motions cease, there is at once a separation... The spirit is then left to itself; and the body, being devoid of the life of its spirit, grows cold and putrescent.

The spirit remains a while in the body after the separation, but only until the total cessation of the heart, which takes place with variety according to the state of disease which was the cause of death. (Continued. See Resuscitate.)
(The drawing of the spirit out of the body. Explained.) HH 449:end.
Man is man from his spirit. (Continued. See Body.)
The reason the spirit does not appear in its human form (before the natural sight). Explained.
Spirits (then) appear in their own form, not only the Spirits who are in the Spiritual World, but also the spirit (of a man), which, being in that World, is still in the body.
The reason the form of the spirit is the human one, is that man as to his spirit has been created after the form of Heaven. Explained.
That the spirit of man, after its solution from the body, is a man, and in a like form. From experience.

When the spirit of a man first enters the World of Spirits, which takes place shortly after his resuscitation, he has a like face and a like tone of voice, because he is then in the state of his exteriors... But afterwards his face becomes quite different; it becomes like his reigning love... in which his spirit had been in the body; for the face of a man's spirit is very different from that of his body, the latter being from his parents, whereas the face of his spirit is from his affection... Into this comes the spirit after (death) in the third state. HH 459, Explained.

Recent Spirits I have Known from their face and speech; but not afterwards... For, regarded in himself, the spirit of a man is nothing but his own affection, the external of which is the face... Hence all who have Known each other (here). Know each other in the World of Spirits; but not in Heaven, nor in Hell.
That (Spirits) possess all sensation, memory, thought, affection... General article.

A Spirit man... sees, hears, speaks, etc. as before; he has appetite, longing and desire; thinks, reflects, is affected, loves, and wills, as before; and he who is delighted with studies, reads and writes as before. In a word, when a man passes from one life into the other... it is as if he had passed from one place to another; and he carries with him all things which he possesses in himself as a man... DLW 176.
Yet the difference between the life of man (as a Spirit) and his life here, is great. Explained.

Everything which a man has thought, willed, spoken, and done, and also which he has heard and seen, is inscribed... on his spirit, and on the members of its body; so that the spirit has been formed according to the thoughts and acts of its will. Fully explained.

When the spirit is in the Spiritual World, it does not think naturally, but spiritually. Hence the natural memory, as to material things, is then quiescent, and those things only come into use which the man has thereby imbibed and made rational. Explained.
Spirits and Angels have a memory equally with men. (Fully quoted under Memory.)
All Spirits can be led wherever one pleases, provided they are kept in their reigning love. They cannot resist it. Explained.
A Spirit is his own reigning love. Explained.
Every man as to his spirit has exteriors and interiors. The exteriors of the spirit are... The interiors of the spirit are...
The life of recent Spirits. Described.
The Spirit man is then let into the state of his interiors. Explained.
Therefore, when the Spirit man is in this state, he is in himself... HH 503, Explained. HH 504, Explained. HH 505, Explained. HH 507.
For Spirits not only think, but also speak, from their own affection.
For the memory of Spirits is in their life... For Spirits are affections, and are in a human form like their affections.
After Spirits have been prepared for Heaven by instructions... they are clothed in angelic garments...
For men are ruled... through Spirits who are in the World of Spirits.
(Thus) the Lord draws away every Spirit to Himself through Angels, and also through influx from Heaven; but Spirits who are in evil resist...
He is then no longer a Spirit man, as he was in his first state; but is truly a Spirit, (that is) he has a face and body which correspond to his internals. Described.
The excellence of Spirits in comparison with men. Explained.

The spirit of a man, while he lives (here) is bound to the body, and through it is in the natural world, and therefore what it then thinks spiritually inflows into natural ideas... But when the spirit is loosed from the body, and comes into its spiritual state... its state as to thoughts and affections immensely excels its former one.
For the spirit of man, when loosed from the body, is in its own good, or evil. Explained.
An Angel or Spirit cannot see anything in the natural world...
Spirits who avert themselves become invisible.
What is not of the love or will of a man is not of his spirit; for the esse of the spirit of a man is love or will.

The conjunction of man with Heaven and with Hell is not immediately with them, but mediately through Spirits who are in the World of Spirits. These Spirits are with man, and none from Hell itself, or Heaven itself.
The Spirits adjoined to man are Subjects. Explained.
The simple have an innate idea that a Spirit is a man.
(References on the subject of the Spirits through whom communications are effected.) NJHD 196.
The will and understanding make the spirit of man... The body is only obedience.
An internal merely natural man... is a Spirit, and not an Angel; and, while he lives in the body, is in society with Spirits, but with those in Hell.
For that only remains in the spirit of a man which has entered into his love. After death all other things are regarded as alien. LJ 36:2.

Angels and Spirits are with man, and in his affections... but they do not know with what men they are; as neither do the men know with what Angels and Spirits they cohabit. The Lord alone knows and disposes this...
So when a man... dies, then, being a Spirit, he does not subsist upon his own proper basis; but upon the general basis, which is the human race.
No Angel or Spirit can subsist without man; and no man without a Spirit and Angel. The conjunction is mutual and reciprocal.
A Spirit in his first state does not know that (he is bound to a Society)... While he is such, he goes hither and thither... and he appears in many other places. (Continued. See Society.)
For the spirit of man... is formed from his will, and from his thought in so far as it proceeds from his will.

The cunning (of the Babylonians) is more malignant there, because they are spirits; and all wickedness stores itself up in the spirit; for the spirit of man is what thinks, wills, intends, and machinates.
Thus they do these things in spirit.
All Spirits and Angels are from the human race.
The quality of any Spirit manifests itself there by influx, which is the communication of his affection. Described.
Spirits and Angels rarely come to the men of Jupiter after they are thirty years old, because they then no longer suffer themselves to be led by them.
Spirits also perceive the Word in its internal sense in so far as their interiors are open into Heaven.
They then receive the idea that the Holy Spirit is the presence of the Lord with man through Angels and Spirits. DLW 150, Explained.
That by spirit is meant the life of man. Explained. DLord 47:2. Illustrated.

Man is said to emit his spirit, when he dies; and therefore by spirit, in this sense, is meant the life of the respiration. Hence, in Hebrew, there is one word for spirit, and wind... It is the life from the respiration of the lungs which is properly meant by spirit, and also by soul.
The life of man is various according to its state, and therefore by spirit is meant the various affection of the life with man. Enumerated, Illustrated.
(By spirit are also meant) the infernal spirits themselves. Illustrated.
By spirit is meant the life of the regenerate, which is called spiritual life. Illustrated.
By spirit is meant spiritual life with those in humiliation. Illustrated.
Where spirit is mentioned in relation to the Lord, His Divine life is meant, thus the Lord Himself. Illustrated.
By spirit,where the Lord is treated of, is meant in special the life of His wisdom, which is Divine Truth. Illustrated.
When the prophets were in vision, they were not in their body, but in their spirit. Illustrated. DP 134.
(Thus) in the Word alone... there is spirit and life. Illustrated.
That Angels and Spirits are men like men here... with the sole difference that they are spiritual... TCR 240.
God and spirit = life from the Lord.
To emit the sour = to animate no longer; and to emit the spirit = to respire no longer.
They are spirit and they are life = (the Divine wisdom and the Divine love).
As to the interiors of his mind, every man is a spirit.

Angels and Spirits are in a totally different light and heat from men... They are not within nature, but entirely above or outside it, and in their own world... They are together with man, conjoined with the affection and thought of his spirit. For man is a Spirit; from this he thinks and wills: and therefore the Spiritual World is where man is, (who) as to the interiors of his mind is in the midst of Angels and Spirits.
As to his spirit, man is in a certain quarter of the Spiritual World.
For, as to his mind, man is a spirit; and, if he is in love and wisdom, he is an Angel; and therefore after death... he becomes a Spirit or an Angel.
Every Spirit turns himself to his reigning love. Explained.
So long as he stays in the World of Spirits, he is called a Spirit...
All the Spirits in the World of Spirits are adjoined to men...
The Spirits below the Heavens appear as if in a cloud.
Hence it is that there is no Spirit or Angel who was not born a man.
Such is the state of Spirits and Angels, who are men, even as to their bodies: they appear in the place where their thought is.
No one can think unless the pulmonary spirit (or breath) concurs and accords. Explained... If he hold his breath, he cannot think, except in his spirit, from its respiration.
The mind of man is his spirit, and the spirit a man; the body being the external through which the mind or spirit sensates and acts in its world. General article. DP 181:2. DP 296:15.
(Origin of the human form of the spirit.)

The conjunction of the spirit with the body is through the correspondence of its will and understanding with its heart and lungs; and the disjunction is through their non-correspondence. General article. DLW 391:end.
The spirit (also) has a pulse and respiration, (which) inflow into those of the body, and produce them. DLW 391:end.
The spirit then goes away and continues its life in the Spiritual World.

When questioned, Spirits and Angels have said that they are as much men as men in the world; that they have a body, and feel the beating of the heart in the breast, and of the arteries on the palm, just as well.
That the spirit of man respires in his body, shown by experience.
I have sometimes been reduced to the respiration of my spirit alone...
Then I was in the spirit, outside the body...
When a man is alone, he thinks from his spirit.
Man is in manifest thought when his spirit thinks in the body... But when he is in the affection of understanding... he is in the thought of his spirit...
The respiration of the spirit depends on fibres from the brains; that of the body on the blood vessels...
As Angels and Spirits are affections... and thoughts... they are not in space and time; but only in the appearance of them...
Hence it is that with every man there are spirits present who are in like affection... and they are as really present as if the man were included in their Society.
Spirits and Angels are affections and derivative thoughts.

Every spirit of a man is affection and the derivative thought; (therefore) every spirit is his own love and thence his own understanding; (so that) when a man is thinking solely from his own spirit... he thinks from the affection of his love; (and it follows) that when a man becomes a Spirit... he is the affection of his own love...
